name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
title: Coupled 2D epithelial sheet
claim: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet relaxes under the Tyssue vertex model and yields finite, uniform per-cell geometry: all 12 cell-faces carry the same basal area (5.0) and the same explicit cell height (1.93), and stepping the EulerSolver keeps that geometry finite. The figure-level comparison of this spatial confinement to the homogeneous R1 baseline, and the explicit BM-traction coupling, are not yet in the composite.
experiment: Build the tyssue_2d_sheet composite (an explicit polygonal CrossSection sheet over the vivarium-tyssue engine, each cell-face carrying an explicit height degree of freedom) and step the EulerSolver. Reconstruct the mesh counts (faces = cells, vertices), read every cell-face basal area and explicit height off face_df, and confirm the geometry stays finite and positive across several Euler steps (dt 0.01). This is a qualitative spatial-engine check -- that the sheet resolves and relaxes to finite per-cell geometry -- not yet a quantitative confinement comparison to R1.
result: The 2D sheet resolves and relaxes deterministically. The mesh carries 12 cell-faces (faces = cells), 12 cells and 24 vertices on a flat z=0 plane spanning +/-5.80 in x and y. Every cell-face relaxes to the same basal area, 5.0, and the same explicit cell height, 1.9319, with all face areas and heights finite. Stepping the EulerSolver five times (dt 0.01) keeps per-cell area and height finite and positive with no NaN or blow-up. The homogeneous cell is uniform because the sheet carries no heterogeneous growth, division or cortical-tension variation yet, and the BM traction/area law is not wired as an explicit coupling -- so the spatial-vs-homogeneous confinement comparison to R1 is a followup, not a result here.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: The explicit 2D sheet resolves over the tyssue engine and relaxes to finite per-cell geometry, so it can serve as the planar spatial substrate the 3D monolayer (R5) builds on. Advancing to the quantitative confinement claim additionally requires the BM-traction coupling and the homogeneous-vs-spatial comparison to R1, which are flagged as followups.

question: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?

purpose.question: Do the paper's confinement regimes survive explicit cell topology and heterogeneous growth in a spatial 2D epithelium?
purpose.mechanism: A Tyssue polygonal sheet carries an explicit per-cell basal area and an explicit cell-height degree of freedom (rather than the inferred prism relation of the homogeneous R1 model). The vertex-model EulerSolver relaxes the sheet; a BM traction/area law (calibrated from R2) is intended to resist basal-area growth, reproducing the R1 confinement response in the homogeneous limit before heterogeneous growth and division are added.
purpose.expected_outcome: The sheet relaxes to finite, well-posed per-cell geometry (areas and heights), establishing the spatial substrate; the homogeneous limit should later match R1's confinement response once the BM traction is coupled.

key_assumptions: The sheet is an explicit polygonal CrossSection: each cell-face carries its own basal area and an explicit cell-height degree of freedom, not an inferred volume/area prism relation.
The current composite is a homogeneous relaxation: no heterogeneous growth, cell division or cortical-tension variation is applied, so all cells relax to the same geometry.
Reduced units throughout (areas, heights, lengths are dimensionless); no calibration to microns is claimed.

The BM traction/area law (calibrated from R2) is NOT wired as an explicit coupling in this composite; the effective constitutive BM and an explicit LAMMPS BM are interchangeable alternatives, not additive forces.
Qualitative scope: this study establishes that the spatial sheet runs and yields finite geometry; the quantitative confinement comparison to R1 is a followup.

model_assumptions_declaration.preferred_vs_realized: explicit — a growing PREFERRED basal area A0(t) drives the cells; the REALIZED area emerges and lags the target under BM resistance (the confinement gap)
model_assumptions_declaration.load_control_vs_reaction: reaction — a reduced-order viscoelastic BM (stiffness + relaxation) resists basal spreading; the resolved vertex-model sheet and an explicit LAMMPS BM are interchangeable alternatives, not additive
model_assumptions_declaration.geometry_dimension: 2D cross-section (a row of prism cells); height reconstructed from a fixed-volume assumption (h = V0/A), not a resolved 3D distance
model_assumptions_declaration.material_representation: reduced-order (effective BM). The resolved vertex-model sheet (tyssue_2d_sheet / CrossSectionGeometry) is a static mesh at the engine level (area does not respond to prefered_area) — a documented limitation
model_assumptions_declaration.growth_vs_division: growth only — a ramped preferred area (linear/exponential); proliferation (cell division) is OFF
model_assumptions_declaration.calibration_limits: reduced units; no micron/pascal/hour calibration; confinement is relative across BM regimes, not an absolute height prediction

meeting_alignment_2026_10_20.note: Highest-priority near-term upgrade (2026-10-20 review). The prior result verified only a viable 2D mesh, not the agreed dynamically-coupled growth experiment. This revision implements a time-varying PREFERRED area distinct from the realized area, with a BM reaction that confines spreading — delivering target A0(t) vs attained A(t), reconstructed height, BM stress, and low/high-stiffness / fast/slow-relaxation comparisons. Growth is a preferred-area ramp (division OFF); real expansion is NOT imposed. The resolved vertex-model planar sheet stays a static substrate at the engine level (named limitation), so the causal experiment runs in the reduced-order 2D cross-section and is labelled as such.

baseline.name: bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium
baseline.note: A 2D epithelial sheet with explicit cell height, relaxed against a basement-membrane area law over the vivarium-tyssue vertex-model engine. It is the spatial counterpart of the homogeneous tissue model, so the confinement response can be read cell by cell rather than for one average cell. The current build relaxes a homogeneous sheet to finite per-cell geometry; heterogeneous growth, division and the explicit BM traction are the next additions.

robustness.note: Deterministic single configuration (one composite, no stochasticity and no parameter variation): the mesh geometry is fixed, so a single relaxation run is the whole evidence. Replication across a BM-stiffness / growth-rate sweep is a gap -- the quantitative confinement comparison to R1 (which does sweep) is a documented followup.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the 2D sheet failed to resolve over the tyssue engine, if any cell-face basal area or explicit height were non-finite or non-positive after relaxation, or if stepping the EulerSolver produced a NaN or a blow-up in the per-cell geometry. Any of these would show the explicit spatial sheet does not yield well-posed geometry. The contracts in tests/test_tyssue_composites.py (test_tyssue_2d_sheet_runs) would fail in that case.

config.title: 2D coupled growth: preferred area → emergent realized area + height
config.caption: MAIN (evidence: observed) — the agreed 2D coupled-growth experiment (2026-10-20 review). A PREFERRED (target) basal area A0(t) grows (proliferation OFF — growth, not cell division); the REALIZED mean area A(t) emerges from the mechanical balance and LAGS the target because a viscoelastic BM resists spreading — that gap IS the confinement, and it is NOT hard-coded to the target. (A) target vs realized area for a free (no-BM) and a stiff/slow BM; (B) reconstructed cell height h = V0/A (a stiff BM confines spreading and drives height up); (C) BM reaction stress across stiffness/relaxation regimes; (D) a BM-stiffness gradient across the row produces a spatial cell-height gradient. Reduced-order 2D CROSS-SECTION of prism cells (the effective-BM realization); height is reconstructed under a declared fixed-volume assumption. Reduced units. NOTE: the resolved vertex-model sheet (tyssue_2d_sheet / CrossSectionGeometry) is a STATIC mesh at the engine level — its area does not respond to prefered_area — so the causal experiment is run in this reduced-order cross-section and the resolved-sheet version remains a named engine limitation.

config.title: R4 — 2D epithelial sheet relaxing (movie)
config.caption: Animated movie of the 12-cell 2D Tyssue sheet relaxing to its finite geometry (edges in blue). Verifies mesh construction; the planar z=0 geometry does not compute a real 3D height (see the quantitative panel + the BM-coupling gap).

config.title: 2D sheet static substrate vs R1 confinement benchmark (demoted)
config.caption: SUPPLEMENT (demoted 2026-10-20) — superseded as the main by the coupled-growth figure above. Documents that the resolved vertex-model tyssue_2d_sheet is a static substrate (all 12 cells relax to the identical basal area 5.0, max vertex displacement ~0) against the R1 confinement benchmark — the engine limitation that motivates running the causal experiment in the reduced-order cross-section. Original caption follows. MAIN (evidence: observed) — NOT a reproduction. Left: the real tyssue_2d_sheet readout over the vivarium-tyssue EulerSolver (dt 0.01) — mean per-cell basal area (fold-change vs step 0) and the stored CrossSection prism-height degree of freedom. Both are flat: all 12 cells relax to the identical basal area (5.0 reduced) and prism-height DOF (1.9319 reduced), and the max vertex displacement over the run is ~0, so the sheet is a pre-equilibrated static mesh with no spatial heterogeneity. Right: the R1 reduced-order prism benchmark (real TissuePrismProcess runs) — the confinement h/h0 trajectory for three BM regimes (soft/fast 0.998->0.38, intermediate 0.998->0.43, stiff/slow 0.998->0.70) — the confinement response the sheet does NOT reproduce. Axes dimensionless (reduced units); single deterministic run (no stochasticity). GAP (named): tyssue_2d_sheet exposes only line_tension + prefered_area — NO BM stiffness / relaxation / traction coupling — so the BM-dependent confinement regimes of Barrientos Fig 1 cannot be produced here; the right panel is the R1 benchmark, not the tyssue sheet.

The geometry is planar (z=0) and does NOT compute a real 3D cell height: the per-face height column is a stored CrossSection prism degree of freedom, not a resolved apical-basal distance. config.title: BM-stiffness-dependent confinement (hypothesis)
config.caption: SUPPLEMENT (evidence: hypothesis) — the BM-stiffness-dependent confinement test the figure review asked for (matched low/high-BM-relaxation cell-sheet snapshots and a basal-area-vs-time panel stratified by BM stiffness, with the R1 benchmark overlaid). NOT producible from tyssue_2d_sheet: its parameters are line_tension + prefered_area, and BM stiffness / relaxation / traction coupling is not wired into the composite. report.title: R4 -- 2D coupled growth: preferred area drives emergent realized area + height
report.verdict: The agreed 2D coupled-growth experiment now runs: a ramped PREFERRED basal area (division OFF) drives a REALIZED area that emerges from the mechanics and lags the target under a viscoelastic BM — a stiff/slow BM lags the target by a 0.317 gap (vs 0.116 free) and raises the reconstructed cell height (0.70→0.91), zero preferred growth gives no BM strain, and a BM-stiffness gradient yields a spatial height gradient (0.76→0.91). This is a reduced-order 2D CROSS-SECTION of prism cells with reconstructed (fixed-volume) height — the effective-BM realization. The resolved vertex-model sheet (tyssue_2d_sheet) is a static mesh at the engine level, so the resolved-sheet and absolute-height claims remain pending.
report.main_insight: PREFERRED-area growth against a viscoelastic BM produces an emergent realized area that lags the target — the lag IS the confinement, not hard-coded — and translates to taller reconstructed cells under a stiffer/slower BM, with spatial BM heterogeneity mapping to spatial cell-shape heterogeneity.
report.caveat: Reduced-order 2D cross-section with reconstructed height (fixed-volume assumption), reduced units; qualitatively consistent with the paper's confinement direction but not a calibrated reproduction. The resolved vertex-model sheet stays a static substrate at the engine level.

followup_proposals.title: Wire the BM traction and compare the 2D sheet's confinement to R1
followup_proposals.motivation: The sheet currently relaxes homogeneously with no explicit BM traction, so it cannot yet test whether the Fig 1 confinement regimes survive explicit topology. Wire the R2-calibrated BM traction/area law, add heterogeneous growth / division / cortical-tension variation, and compare the per-cell confinement response to the homogeneous R1 baseline.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: An explicit BM traction resisting basal-area growth should reproduce R1's confinement in the homogeneous limit and introduce spatial force/area heterogeneity under growth.

resolved_uncertainties: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet resolves over the tyssue engine and relaxes to finite, well-posed per-cell geometry.
The spatial sheet is numerically stable over short EulerSolver integration (no NaN / blow-up).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the Fig 1 confinement regimes survive explicit topology -- needs the BM traction coupling and heterogeneous growth.
